# Yang Shao for Alameda County Water District Board, Ward 3
# Yang Shao
The Best Candidate for Alameda County Water District Board, Ward 3
## I love our Tri-City community, but the families of Fremont, Newark, and Union City are being squeezed by a cost-of-living crisis — and your water bill is part of the problem.
Rates have gone up every single year, 63% since 2017, and now the Alameda County Water District approved back-to-back 5% increases for 2027 and 2028 — more than 79% in 12 years*, far outpacing family paychecks.
These increases are not inevitable. They are the result of spending that goes unexamined, financing decisions that go unquestioned, and a board culture where rate hikes pass year after year without real scrutiny. Ratepayers are asked to conserve more and pay more, while the district’s expenditures — including the State Water Project taxes collected on your property bill — remain difficult for ordinary residents to see and understand.
Clean, safe, and affordable water is an essential public service, not a blank check. Our district needs a course correction: independent oversight, genuine transparency, and a director who puts ratepayers first.
* ACWD Board Meeting and Workshop Records
Board Meeting | Paul Sethy Voted Yes
Jan. 12, 2012 | Commodity +6%, meter service charge +19%, about +8% for the average home, effective Feb. 1, 2012
Feb. 9, 2017 | Commodity and meter service charge +20% for 2017 and another +5% for 2018, effective March 1, 2017 and March 1, 2018
Feb. 7, 2019 | Commodity and meter service charge +4%, effective March 1, 2019
Feb. 10, 2022 | meter service charge +6%, commodity unchanged, about 2% for the average customer, effective March 1, 2022
Feb. 9, 2023 | Commodity and meter service charge +4% for two years, effective March 1, 2023 and March 1, 2024
Feb. 13, 2025 | Commodity and meter service charge +4% for two years, effective March 1, 2025 and March 1, 2026
July 30, 2026 (workshop) | Commodity and meter service charge +5% for two years
### The Most Experienced and Accomplished Candidate for Ward 3
As a 23-year Fremont resident, a Fremont City Councilmember for eight years, and a Fremont Unified School District Trustee for four, I have always focused on measurable results — not slogans or political theater. Working together with our community, Fremont has become a model of what effective, accountable local governance can achieve.
Under our collective leadership, Fremont has been recognized as:
- The Happiest City in the United States for six consecutive years
- Best Place to Raise a Family in America for four consecutive years
- One of the Top Ten Greenest Cities in the United States
- The Safest City in Northern California
- A city delivering thousands of units of affordable housing while balancing growth with quality of life
Fremont’s success did not happen by accident. It is the result of disciplined governance, data-driven decision-making, and a steadfast commitment to fiscal responsibility and community well-being.
I also bring something rare to a water board: I am a scientist, with a Harvard Ph.D. in Chemistry. That means the technical expertise to scrutinize water quality data, review infrastructure plans line by line, and stop wasteful capital spending before it lands on your bill. These are the same principles — and the same results-oriented approach — that I will bring to the Alameda County Water District.
Yang Shao’s Priorities for ACWD
### Rate Relief
Reject the approved back-to-back 5% hikes and break the cycle of automatic annual increases — through independent audits, smart project financing, and fixed-charge reform, so every household that conserves water sees real savings.
### Real Transparency
Publish clear, plain-language accounting of all district spending, including Meter Service Charge and the State Water Project taxes on your property bill. Ratepayers deserve to know where every dollar goes.
### Reliable Infrastructure
Replace aging pipelines and protect our local groundwater basin proactively — before main breaks force costly emergency repairs. Smart planning today prevents expensive crises tomorrow.
### A Proven Voice, Broad Support
I believe our water district needs problem-solvers, not politics. I am honored to have earned the support of elected officials, community leaders, and neighbors across Fremont, Newark, and Union City who share a simple belief: ratepayers deserve a director who listens, delivers, and demands real answers.
## Together, we can bring accountability, transparency, and rate relief to the Alameda County Water District — and ensure clean, safe, affordable water for every family in our community.
I humbly ask for your vote for ACWD Board of Directors, Ward 3.

If you contribute by check, please make the check out to “Yang Shao for ACWD Ward 3 Director 2026 FPPC# 1496542” and mail it to:
Yang Shao for ACWD Ward 3 Director 2026
41041 Trimboli Way #1152
Fremont, CA 94538
If you contribute by Zelle, send money to yangshao4acwd
Contribution Rules:
There is a $5,900 contribution limit per person per election cycle for ACWD Director.
Contributions are not tax-deductible for income tax purposes.
Election law requires us to publicly report cumulative contributions of $100 or more. We may not accept contributions from individual donors without their name, street address, and occupation and employer information.
In making this contribution, the contributor affirms that he/she is a United States citizen or a permanent resident alien.
There are exceptions for some types of political parties and committees.
